_comment: The ground the maps are drawn on, and where it came from.
ONE FILE, NOT A BASEMAP SERVICE. A tile service would put a third party in the
render path of every page, hand it a log of who read what, and make the map's
appearance something this repository does not control. A vector file in the tree
is a fact this repo holds, versioned with everything else, and the map it draws
is the same map in five years.
WHY ADMIN 0 COUNTRIES AND NOT A COASTLINE FILE. The maps need coastline AND
national borders, and this one file carries both: the polygon boundaries are the
coast where they meet water and the border where they meet another country. A
separate coastline layer would have to be drawn against these polygons anyway and
would disagree with them at every simplified headland.
WHY 1:10m AND NOT 1:50m. The project pages crop to a few hundred kilometres
around one plant. At 1:50m a fjord is a notch and the Danish islands are a smear,
which on a regional crop reads as a drawing error rather than as a simplification.
At Europe-wide zoom 1:10m costs nothing that the render pipeline cannot simplify
back out. The trade is one direction only: detail can be dropped later, and
cannot be added.
PUBLIC DOMAIN. Natural Earth places its data in the public domain and asks for no
attribution. The site will credit it anyway, because a map that does not say what
it is drawn from is a map nobody can check.
The zip is committed as fetched, unmodified, with its checksum below. Anything
derived from it — a clipped, simplified, projected GeoJSON for the browser — is a
build output and is generated from this file, never hand-edited.
title: Natural Earth — Admin 0 Countries, 1:10m
